identity.rationale: The selected paper connects oil-fired residue to heavy-fuel-oil combustion but does not report the sample collection fraction needed to call this feed specifically fly ash. Its Tehran plant is unnamed; Neka provenance from a different incompletely inspected RSC source is not borrowed.
identity.organism: Source-reported Aspergillus niger PTCC 5210 purchased from IROST. Current PTCC accession authority not independently resolved; no strain CURIE invented.
identity.criticality: Not asserted; constituent elements and resource are distinct.

claims_and_limits: Actual ash milled and screened below 75 micrometres; study provenance is a Tehran thermal power plant, not an authenticated Neka sample.

PTCC 5210 culture, 100 g/L sucrose medium ; 14-day flask growth at 30 degrees C / 130 rpm versus 7-day 1-L bubble-column growth at 30 degrees C / 760 mL/min. Source inoculum count 10^7 has no stated volume denominator or final inoculum fraction.
Biomass removal stated but method and residual-cell test absent; subsequent ash contact at 3% w/v, 60 degrees C, 7 days. Culture working volume is not leaching-vessel volume.

Figure 2 and Results report 97% V / 50% Ni for flask spent medium and 100% V / 33% Ni for reactor spent medium. These are source-reported extraction values, not independently reconstructed or isolated-product yields.

No liquid-metal assay, sampling fraction, yield equation, replication count or Figure 2 uncertainty is described. Figure 1 agar-growth error bars are undefined and do not constitute an ash-leaching control.

No matched sterile-medium, pure-acid or pH-controlled leach comparison. Acid-rich culture fluids and reported leaching support an association; unique acid causality and microbial enhancement are not established.

Proposed nickel oxalate is not identified in Figure 3, which labels NiO in treated ash. Text emphasizes an iron sulfate residue but the plotted treated assignments include other phases. No complete V removal, single-phase residue, quantified porosity, safe reuse, product recovery or industrial deployment is inferred.
Biomass accumulation caused aeration difficulty for longer reactor cultivation. Unequal culture times/media histories preclude a general scale-superiority claim.
